name: Web Components | a11y-elements
tagline: Framework-agnostic accessibility Custom Elements: a behavior layer for real markup, not a themed UI kit.
popTagline: Built to stop rewriting the same accessibility behavior in every project.
popOverview: A framework-agnostic library of accessible Web Components, providing reusable interface elements and interaction patterns without imposing a framework or design system. Built around native browser capabilities, it aims to make accessible interfaces easier to integrate and customize.

sectionKeyPoints.Component library: Around 30 custom elements covering form controls, navigation, images, loading states and overlays.

sectionKeyPoints.Form validation: Native form validation enhanced with custom validators, contextual errors and reusable field components.

sectionKeyPoints.Overlays: A complete set of overlay patterns: modals, drawers, dropdowns, tooltips, notifications and more.

sectionKeyPoints.Framework-agnostic by design: A behavior layer rather than a themed UI kit, usable with vanilla JavaScript or any frontend framework.

sectionKeyPoints.Light DOM architecture: No shadow DOM, keeps the underlying markup accessible and directly styleable.

sectionKeyPoints.Native-first: Form controls remain the source of truth, while documented CSS custom properties and an opt-in dark theme leave presentation in the developer's hands.

sectionKeyPoints.Consistency: Implementing consistent keyboard interaction and focus management across different browsers, components and interaction patterns.

sectionKeyPoints.Handling complex overlay behavior: Focus containment and restoration, background inertness, dismissal rules and screen-reader announcements.

sectionKeyPoints.Reliability: Maintaining reliable distribution across modular ESM imports and standalone browser bundles, with a test suite covering 700+ tests across 50 files.
